questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Close to my home university, which is Copenhagen University.
A relative warm location, with good food. 
The posibilities to travel and explore.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. But it all worked out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was created a Whatsapp group, and the university send some information by mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Not very easy at all.
I wanted to have my own appartement, which i found by AirBnb. 
I booked several places, but they kept being cancelled. 
Finally I found a place, which was very expensive, but okay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university do offer housing, for an example at Martinit. Some of my friends lived there, and they liked it a lot.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university did not help me find the courses at all, and some courses did not match the description.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Expect to have 5 courses of 6 ECTS points.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Some courses were to easy and some to hard. 
Some professors was also very bad.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
How long were you on exchange? *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Time Series Analysis (Econometrics II), Game theory (Micro Economics III), Business History (Economic History) and New Business Start-Up.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I reccomend all but New Business Start-Up, as the professor was terrible. Do NOT take this class with MArio Benassi.

questions.answer: Not unexpected, but i spent a lot of money travelling around in Italy.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks can be very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel, Travel and Travel.
We rented a Van with IndieCampers, and travelled around a weekend, which was a lot of fun.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Relax, Milan is an amazing city with amazing people.
Save money for traveling. 
Enjoy!!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding the right courses, and passing them ;)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Milan is awesome. The city is great, the people are sweet, and the food&drinks are the best!
There are crazy football matches, parties all night and beautifull arhitecture. 
Endless opportunities to travel, and the italian culture is remarkeble.
